{{Short description|Principle in set theory}}

In mathematical set theory, the '''axiom of adjunction''' states that for any two sets ''x'', ''y'' there is a set ''w''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''x''&nbsp;∪&nbsp;{''y''} given by "adjoining" the set ''y'' to the set ''x''. It is stated as

:<math>\forall x. \forall y. \exists w. \forall z. \big( z \in w \leftrightarrow (z \in x \lor z=y) \big).</math>

{{harvs|txt|last=Bernays|authorlink=Paul Bernays|year=1937|loc=page 68, axiom II (2)}} introduced the axiom of adjunction as one of the axioms for a system of set theory that he introduced in about 1929.
It is a weak axiom, used in some weak systems of set theory such as [[general set theory]] or [[finitary set theory]]. The adjunction operation is also used as one of the operations of [[primitive recursive set function]]s.

== Interpretability of arithmetic ==
[[Alfred Tarski|Tarski]] and [[Wanda Szmielew|Szmielew]] showed that [[Robinson arithmetic]] (<math>{\mathsf{Q}}</math>) can be interpreted in a weak set theory whose axioms are [[extensionality]], the existence of the empty set, and the axiom of adjunction {{harv|Tarski|1953|loc=p.34}}.
In fact, in the language of set theory extended with a function symbol for adjunction, the axioms of empty set and adjunction alone (without extensionality) suffice to interpret <math>{\mathsf{Q}}</math>.<ref>{{cite journal
| last1      = Mancini
| first1     = Antonella
| last2      = Montagna
| first2     = Franco
| date       = Spring 1994
| title      = A minimal predicative set theory
| url        = https://projecteuclid.org/journals/notre-dame-journal-of-formal-logic/volume-35/issue-2/A-minimal-predicative-set-theory/10.1305/ndjfl/1094061860.full
| journal    = Notre Dame Journal of Formal Logic
| volume     = 35
| issue      = 2
| pages      = 186–203
| doi        = 10.1305/ndjfl/1094061860
| access-date = 23 November 2021
| doi-access= free
| url-access= subscription
}}</ref> (They are mutually interpretable.)

Adding [[epsilon-induction]] to empty set and adjunction yields a theory that is mutually interpretable with [[Peano arithmetic]] (<math>{\mathsf{PA}}</math>).
Another [[axiom schema]] also yields a theory that is mutually interpretable with <math>{\mathsf{PA}}</math>:<ref>{{cite web
| url          = https://cpb-us-w2.wpmucdn.com/u.osu.edu/dist/1/1952/files/2014/01/GodelLect060202-n2gdjc.pdf
| title        = Issues in the foundations of mathematics
| last         = Friedman
| first        = Harvey M.
| author-link  = Harvey M. Friedman
| date         = June 2, 2002
| website      = Department of Mathematics
| publisher    = Ohio State University
| access-date  = January 18, 2023}}</ref>
:<math>\forall x. \forall y. \exists w. \forall z. \Big(z \in w \leftrightarrow \big((z \in x \lor z = y) \land \phi\big)\Big)</math>, 
where <math>\phi</math> is not allowed to have <math>w</math> free. This combines axioms of set theory: For <math>\phi</math> trivially true it reduced to the adjunction axiom above, and for <math>(z\neq y)\land P</math> it gives the [[axiom of separation]] with <math>P</math>.
